input_note: ImageNet-normalised RGB CHW — BGR to RGB, /255, then mean/std. The normalisation is on the host (BCDL's anomalyPreprocess), hence `no_preprocess`; the graph takes the already-normalised tensor.

outputs.anomaly_map: 1x36x36 coarse anomaly map; the host upsamples to the input resolution and applies a Gaussian blur
outputs.note: The IMAGE score is the map's MAXIMUM, not its mean. How bad a part is depends on its worst patch, and a mean lets a large clean area hide a small defect — which is the case the method exists to catch.

quantisation: compiler default (predominantly int8). Measured, not assumed — see cosine and task_metric.

licence.detail: Code and released weights are MIT. The shipped checkpoint is trained on MVTec AD, which is CC BY-NC-SA 4.0: attribution, no commercial use, and derivatives under the same terms. Unlike a bare 'research only' notice, a Creative Commons licence has an explicit framework for adapted material, so a model trained on it may be redistributed under the same licence — the same reading applied to ViTPose (MAE, CC-BY-NC-4.0). Note the SHARE-ALIKE, which ViTPose does not carry: a redistributed .hbm should travel under CC BY-NC-SA 4.0. IMPORTANT AND EASY TO MISS: this restriction does NOT reach a real deployment. A deployed GLASS is retrained on the customer's own normal parts, so it derives from their data, not from MVTec's. What is encumbered is this example checkpoint, not the capability.

toolchain.note: The host HBDK and the board HBRT must match; 3.7.0 host pairs with 4.0.5 board.

cosine.note: A is ONNX against torch: cosine 1.0. B is the int8 .hbm against the float ONNX — and 0.9409 is far below any usual gate while costing NOTHING on the task metric. AUROC is rank-based: quantisation noise moves every score slightly and does not reorder them. Read this next to the neuflow recipe, where 0.9954 hid an unusable model. Cosine is not a proxy for task quality in EITHER direction.

task_metric.name: image-level and pixel-level AUROC on the product's own test set
task_metric.protocol: MVTec-AD `bottle` test split, 83 images with pixel-level ground-truth masks. Feed the board and the float ONNX the identical 288x288 BGR input; the board runs BCDL's own preprocessing.
task_metric.threshold: image and pixel AUROC within ~0.002 of the float model
task_metric.measured: float ONNX 0.9905 image / 0.9907 pixel; int8 .hbm 0.9905 / 0.9905; int16 0.9897 / 0.9905. Best F1 0.984, pixel IoU 0.668.
task_metric.note: The practical caveat the AUROC hides: good and defective scores OVERLAP (best normal 0.953 against worst defect 0.882). Zero misses costs ~50% false alarms; zero false alarms misses ~5%. The misses are all `contamination` — small foreign objects. THE THRESHOLD IS A LINE-SIDE DECISION, not a property of the model.

measured.note: S100P, hrt_model_exec perf, thread_num 1, min of 3 runs on a board gated against its own recorded numbers.

rejected_builds.name: set_all_nodes_int16
rejected_builds.why: No accuracy to buy: 0.9897 image AUROC against int8's 0.9905, i.e. marginally worse on the metric that matters, at a larger model. A LATENCY comparison published earlier ("91x slower") was WRONG and is withdrawn — it was measured on a contaminated board where the same model varied 46x between back-to-back runs. Any int8/int16 latency ratio must be re-measured min-of-N on a quiet board.

graph_rewrites.why: The BPU does not support Unfold, so this was expected to need a rewrite.
graph_rewrites.verified: It needed none: the torch exporter lowers it into standard operators. After onnxslim the graph is 136 nodes with NO red-flag operator — only Conv, Relu, Pool, Reshape, Transpose, Gemm, MatMul, Sigmoid.

graph_rewrites.op: batch and resolution fixed at 1 x 288 x 288
graph_rewrites.why: Upstream's exporter defaults to a dynamic batch; the graph must be static.

board_verification.note: Compiled and board-verified against the official MVTec-AD `bottle` test set with pixel-level ground truth (see task_metric). 72.6 ms BPU of an 81.0 ms end-to-end; preprocessing is 1.6 ms and decode 6.8 ms, of which 6.3 ms is the Gaussian blur (`blur_kernel=0` skips it but then diverges from the reference post-processing).
board_verification.to_go_faster: Change the backbone. 72.6 ms is a WideResNet-50 at 288x288 and that is the whole cost. Lean GLASS (MobileNetV2 backbone) is the ready-made next step.
board_verification.not_done: Only `bottle` was trained and converted. Every other MVTec category is a separate checkpoint through the same recipe.
